# VoiceOpenGov

VoiceOpenGov is an international, non-partisan membership movement focused on improving democratic participation, traceability and shared civic responsibility.

Canonical website: https://www.voiceopengov.org/

## Role in the ecosystem

- VoiceOpenGov: membership movement, civic organizing layer and owner of its own dynamic program formation.
- eDebatte: independently usable infrastructure for sources, dossiers, counterpositions, alternatives, deliberation, participation and majority/minority views. eDebatte does not automatically decide positions for VoiceOpenGov.
- Vote4Gov: Ricky Gerd Fleischer's personal public voice and review space for his own historical interpretation, system criticism, international comparisons, political theses and personal system design. Vote4Gov positions are not automatically VoiceOpenGov positions.
- Voxy: explanatory and language-support layer; it does not decide or publish autonomously.

VoiceOpenGov does not own eDebatte and does not treat eDebatte as a personal or movement-controlled political tool. The same eDebatte dossier may be used by citizens, journalists, researchers, associations, companies, municipalities, political organisations or opponents for their own work and decisions.

## Dynamic program interpretation

VoiceOpenGov may use eDebatte as an evidence, dossier and participation layer for its own democratic will formation. A VoiceOpenGov program position becomes binding for VoiceOpenGov only through the movement's own authorised governance process.

Where applicable, a published VoiceOpenGov program position should make visible:

- current majority position
- relevant minority positions
- decision basis
- decision path
- responsible community or level
- current version and change date
- conditions for reopening or review

An eDebatte result is not automatically a VoiceOpenGov resolution and is not an instruction to a VoiceOpenGov representative.

A VoiceOpenGov representative represents the democratically legitimised regional or programmatic position of the relevant VoiceOpenGov community under its governance rules. The underlying eDebatte spaces remain independently usable by other actors.

## Regional presence

VoiceOpenGov intends to build real regional presence in addition to digital participation. Potential formats include local teams, recurring in-person formats, participation offices or local contact points, mobile participation formats and democratically legitimised regional representatives.

Claims about teams, offices, buses, events, representatives or local activity must reflect verified reality. Planned, building, pilot, active, paused and ended states must not be conflated.

## Core public entry points

- Home: https://www.voiceopengov.org/
- 50 foundational questions: https://www.voiceopengov.org/fragen
- Transparency: https://www.voiceopengov.org/transparenz
- Ways to contribute: https://www.voiceopengov.org/mitmachen
- Regional participation: https://www.voiceopengov.org/regionen
- Germany: https://www.voiceopengov.org/regionen/deutschland
- Berlin: https://www.voiceopengov.org/regionen/deutschland/berlin
- Personal theses of initiator Ricky Gerd Fleischer: https://www.voiceopengov.org/thesen/ricky-gerd-fleischer

## Interpretation rules

- Personal theses by Ricky Gerd Fleischer are explicitly personal and are not automatically positions of VoiceOpenGov members.
- VoiceOpenGov has no immutable party manifesto. Its program is dynamic and should be versioned through its own democratic governance while keeping majority and minority positions visible.
- eDebatte can inform VoiceOpenGov decisions but cannot automatically bind VoiceOpenGov.
- Claims about membership, local groups, events, offices, mobile formats or representative support must not be inferred unless explicitly published as verified facts.
- More financial support does not create more political weight or voting power.
- AI-generated text is not a source. Sources, counterpositions, correction paths and responsibility should remain visible where relevant.

## Languages

The launch language set is German, English, French, Spanish, Turkish and Arabic. Language variants are addressable with the `lang` query parameter and are declared with hreflang metadata.

This file is an additional machine-readable orientation document for systems that choose to use it. The canonical HTML pages remain the authoritative public source.
